220-langue-et-litterature-francaises: Take PHIL 344 or POLI 334, not both.
220-program-description: Film aesthetics, history and theory across national and international traditions, drawing on teaching in several Arts departments.
221-complementary-courses-12-credits: At least 6 on non-U.S. cinemas, at most 6 from one department, and at most 6 from the discipline of your other programs.
222-environment: See Bieler (p. 821): a Minor open to everyone, the B.A. Faculty Program, Honours for senior students, a Joint Honours component, and a Diploma for those with a degree.
223-about-french-as-a-second-language: Open to any program, for careers or for further study in French. Arts Foundation students in the En français option may take up to 18 FRSL credits.
223-admission-and-registration: A placement test is needed for every FRSL course, including beginners', with a high school or CEGEP transcript ready. The Centre gives permission once your level is set, or directs you to the French department or Continuing Studies.

Tests run through the year until places fill. Places are limited and first-come, with no auditors. Attend every class in the first two weeks or lose your spot. You may be moved if your level doesn't fit.
223-student-affairs-office: Arts Building, Room 155, 853 Sherbrooke St. W.
224-about-gender-sexuality-feminist-and-: Interdisciplinary study of gender, sexuality and feminism through social justice, including critical race, disability and Indigenous studies.
224-location: 3487 Peel St., 2nd Floor. Adviser: Si Yu Li.
224-program-description: Current and historical issues in gender, sexuality, feminism and justice, and how gender, race, class, identity, age, ability and citizenship shape power.
224-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3 credits, then 3 GSFS, then 12 from the wider list, at least 6 at 300+, each engaging at least two of the four themes. Credits count once. At most 3 from approved exchange.
226-program-description: GSFS courses for immersion, plus complementaries across faculties. See an adviser when declaring and before your final year.
Take GSFS 200 and 250 in first year, GSFS 300 in second, GSFS 400 in final year.
226-complementary-courses-24-credits: 9 from the GSFS list, 3 at 400–500. 15 from the wider list, at least 3 at 400–500 and at most 9 at 200, engaging two themes. At most 12 from exchange.
226-gender-sexuality-feminist-and-social: Credits count once. Listed courses count only when they centrally engage at least two of the themes.
228-program-description: Deeper analysis, research and seminars, ending in an Honours thesis with a supervisor approved the year before, and a Colloquium with extra reading, methods training and presentations. Keep program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00.
GSFS 200 and 250 in first year, GSFS 300 in second, GSFS 495D and 496D in your last full year. See an adviser on registering and before your final year.
229-complementary-courses-39-credits: 9 from the GSFS list, 3 at 400–500. 30 from the wider list, at least 9 at 400–500 and at most 12 at 200, engaging two themes. At most 12 from exchange.
229-gender-sexuality-feminist-and-social: Credits count once, and only courses centrally engaging two themes are accepted.
231-complementary-courses-21-credits: 9 from the GSFS list, 3 at 400–500. 12 from the wider list, at least 3 at 400–500 and at most 9 at 200, engaging two themes. At most 12 from exchange.
231-gender-sexuality-feminist-and-social: Credits count once, and only courses centrally engaging two themes are accepted.
233-about-geography: Both natural and social science, connecting people and environment. Human Geography looks at political, economic and cultural processes in places; Physical Geography draws on climatology, geomorphology, hydrology, ecology and more.
Leads to environmental consulting, social agencies and NGOs, with marketable GIS skills, or graduate work in social sciences, urban planning and environment.
233-programs-offered: B.A. (including Urban Studies), B.Sc. (p. 1197) and B.A. & Sc. (p. 516).
233-interdepartmental-major-in-earth-sys: With Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences and Earth and Planetary Sciences (p. 1186). Adviser: William (Bill) Minarik.
233-field-study-semesters: Through Science's Internship and Field Studies Office or McGill Abroad.
233-mcgill-east-africa-field-study-semes: The local environment and the goals and challenges of people in East Africa.
233-mcgill-barbados-field-study-semester: At Bellairs, on the UN Sustainable Development Goals and small island states.
233-mcgill-panama-field-study-semester: With the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, on Latin America's social and tropical environmental issues.
233-location: Burnside Hall, Floors 3–7, 805 Sherbrooke St. W. Administrative Office: Room 305.
234-undergraduate-advisor: Michelle Maillet, Academic Associate, Burnside Hall, Room 322.
234-program-description: People, places and environment, a good complement to many majors. Expands into the Geography Major, not the Urban Studies one.
234-program-description-2: Urban dynamics and challenges worldwide. Follow course levels: 200 in U1, 300 in U2, 400–500 in U3.
235-architecture: Prerequisites are waived for Urban Studies students, but 500-level waits until U3.
235-program-description: Fundamentals of geospatial tools. 6 credits required.
235-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3, 3 and 6 credits from three lists, with no double-counting.
236-program-description: Health results from individuals and their physical and social environments, and outcomes differ widely by place. Local and global issues, with spatial and statistical skills.
236-complementary-courses-6-credits: 3 credits from each list. May have prerequisites. PPHS 525 or SOCI 525.
236-program-description-2: People, places and environment, through human and physical geography, methods and field work.
237-statistics: Credit is limited; see Course Overlap in Arts' Course Requirements.
237-geography: 18 GEOG credits, not GEOG 200 or 205, at least 3 at 400+.
237-program-description: Approaches to studying the urban world and methods. Follow course levels. Up to 30 credits may be outside Arts and Science.
238-remaining-courses: 21 credits, at least 15 at 300+ and at least 6 outside Geography.
239-program-description: Adds coursework and a two-semester original research project under a supervisor, normally in final year. Keep CGPA 3.00 and program GPA 3.30.
